clue.text: See 8
Revealing top error, public transport

parts.note: a boob is a silly blunder
the Tube is London's underground railway

explanation.surface: A gaffe made on a crowded bus or train.
explanation.walkthrough: The TUBE is the everyday name for the London Underground.
explanation.definitionFit: A boob tube is a strapless, tight elastic garment worn on the upper body, so it shows a lot of skin.

clue.text: Drink second short

indicators.note: short means the word is cut back by its final letter

parts.note: the latter is the second of two things mentioned

explanation.surface: Someone orders a quick drink for a moment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' removes the last letter, R, from LATTER.
explanation.definitionFit: A latte is a coffee made with lots of steamed milk, a familiar café beverage.

clue.text: 1/0 feeble odds, awfully slow work at the same time

parts.note: 1 is the Roman numeral I and 0 is nothing, NONE

indicators.note: the odd-numbered letters, first, third and fifth, are taken from the word feeble
awfully suggests the word slow is badly put together, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: OP is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: A gambler bemoans weak odds and slow progress all at once.
explanation.walkthrough: '1/0' is read as the Roman one followed by nothing at all; 'awfully' gives LSWO. The definition is the idiom's sense, not its words.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means all in one sudden action, so everything happens simultaneously.

clue.text: Crusader's companion overcoming infidels initially with a plant

indicators.note: in a down entry one piece sitting over another means it comes first

parts.note: Batman, the Caped Crusader, has Robin as his sidekick

indicators.note: initially means just the opening letter of the word infidels

explanation.surface: A medieval knight's comrade defeats unbelievers and carries a plant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crusader' looks medieval but is the Caped Crusader, Batman, whose partner is Robin. 'initially' gives I from infidels.
explanation.definitionFit: Robinia is a genus of trees and shrubs that includes the false acacia, a kind of plant.

clue.text: Leads written up about paper that's shot

indicators.note: about means the reins piece goes around the paper piece
in a down entry written up means read from bottom to top, so backwards

parts.note: leads that guide a horse are reins
FT is the Financial Times newspaper

explanation.surface: A news headline reports that a newspaper reporter has been shot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'written up' gives SNIER. 'shot' looks like gunfire but is a small drink.
explanation.definitionFit: A snifter is a small tot of spirits, the same as a shot of something strong.

clue.text: A slow type, quick as you can!

parts.note: a sap is a foolish, slow-witted person

explanation.surface: Someone urges a slowcoach to hurry up.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition plays against 'slow' in the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: The abbreviation stands for 'as soon as possible', a demand for speed.

clue.text: Calm around government's leadership? It's going the other way, that's plain

indicators.note: the calm piece goes around the single letter taken from government

parts.note: calm means serene

indicators.note: leadership means the leading, first letter of the word
going the other way means the word it is read backwards

parts.note: the word it, with its 's read as is

explanation.surface: A political question about calm leadership turning the other way.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark covers 'leadership' meaning a first letter rather than political leaders; 'going the other way' is the reversal.
explanation.definitionFit: The Serengeti is a vast grassland in Tanzania, a famous example of an open plain.

clue.text: Ailing during dip, king pulled out of backstroke, swimming in pool

indicators.note: the word ailing sits inside the word dip, as one event happens within another
letters that are swimming move about freely, so the pool of pieces is rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: one letter is withdrawn from the word backstroke

parts.note: K is the chess abbreviation for king
ailing means ill

explanation.surface: A swimmer feeling ill on a dip has to give up the backstroke in the pool.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pulled out of' leaves BACSTROKE; 'swimming' shuffles it with DIP into POCKETBIARDS, and 'during' sets ILL inside. 'pool' looks like the swimming bath but is the table game.
explanation.definitionFit: Pocket billiards is the American name for the cue game played on a table with six pockets, otherwise called pool.

clue.text: A colonic ailment less constant, requiring treatment that's soothing

indicators.note: letters needing treatment are worked on and rearranged
less means one letter is taken away from the fodder

parts.note: c is the symbol for a constant, such as the speed of light

explanation.surface: A digestive complaint needs soothing medical treatment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'less' removes one C from A COLONIC AILMENT, and 'requiring treatment' shuffles the fourteen letters left.
explanation.definitionFit: Calamine lotion is a pink skin preparation applied to calm itching and sunburn.

clue.text: Beat cheat that's passed away

parts.note: something out has gone, as a fire that is out has died
to do someone is to swindle them

explanation.surface: Beating a dead swindler.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the clue as a swindle that is finished, a cheat that has passed away, so the 'passed away' word comes first.
explanation.definitionFit: To outdo someone is to surpass or defeat them.

clue.text: Writer pens right magic word, only somewhat odd stuff

indicators.note: pens means encloses, so the writer piece holds the letter for right

parts.note: Bic is a brand of ballpoint pen

indicators.note: only somewhat means just part of the magic word is used, its ending dropped

parts.note: abracadabra is the conjuror's magic word

explanation.surface: A ballpoint holds the right spell, only partly, among odds and ends.
explanation.walkthrough: 'only somewhat' keeps ABRAC, the first five letters of the spell.
explanation.definitionFit: Bric-a-brac means miscellaneous ornaments and curios of small value, a mixed collection of things.

clue.text: Metal-plated present inside

indicators.note: plated means covered, so the metal surrounds the other piece

parts.note: tin is a metal
present means here

explanation.surface: A gift wrapped in metal plating, tucked inside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'present' looks like a gift but is the adverb meaning in this place.
explanation.definitionFit: Therein is a formal word meaning in that place or thing.

clue.text: Plane perhaps carrying first of applicants in for The Apprentice

indicators.note: carrying means holding the other pieces inside

parts.note: the plane is a kind of tree, so a tree is defined by example

indicators.note: first of means the opening letter of the word applicants

explanation.surface: An aircraft brings in a candidate for the television show The Apprentice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plane' suggests an aircraft but is the plane tree; 'carrying' holds A plus IN.
explanation.definitionFit: A trainee is a learner in a job, much like an apprentice.

clue.text: Shift work in retail going up, their prices down

parts.note: to budge is to shift slightly

indicators.note: work here means the letters are worked into new order

explanation.surface: A shift worker in shops sees costs rise while others fall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'work' gives TAIRLINE; 'Shift work' poses as a job pattern. The definition plays on planes rising while fares fall.
explanation.definitionFit: A budget airline is a cheap carrier whose planes take to the air while fares stay low.

clue.text: Bishop wearing expensive jewellery keeping away

indicators.note: the bishop is wearing, or inside, the word for expensive

parts.note: dear means expensive
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop
a ring is a piece of jewellery

explanation.surface: A bishop in costly jewels is barred.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wearing' makes DEBAR; the surface pictures a bejewelled cleric.
explanation.definitionFit: Debarring means excluding or banning, keeping someone out.

clue.text: For example, pay good after a raise for chef's assistant

parts.note: EG is short for exempli gratia, for example

indicators.note: in a down entry a raise means read upwards, so the word for pay is reversed

parts.note: to remit is to send payment

explanation.surface: A worker gets a good pay rise for helping a chef.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a raise' turns REMIT into TIMER, which ends the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An egg timer is a small sand glass or clock used by cooks to time boiling eggs.

clue.text: 8 1 across, it's suggested? That's not cricket!

definitions.meaning: playing pool with one's hands in one's trouser pockets is a jocular euphemism for fiddling with oneself
illegally altering the condition of the ball is cheating in cricket

explanation.walkthrough: Cross-references read 8 and 1 across together, the cue game, here a schoolboy slang euphemism. Cricket is the British bat-and-ball sport.
explanation.definitionFit: Ball-tampering is the cricket offence of scuffing or shining the ball illegally to make it swing.

clue.text: Brown off to buttonhole Blair once for a high post

indicators.note: to buttonhole someone is to hold them close, so the brown piece holds the other inside

parts.note: to toast bread is to brown it off
Tony Blair was once Prime Minister, PM

explanation.surface: Gordon Brown leaves to corner former leader Tony Blair over a top job.
explanation.walkthrough: Brown and Blair suggest the two Labour prime ministers; Brown is the colour, toast.
explanation.definitionFit: A topmast is the upper section of a ship's mast, a tall wooden pole.

clue.text: Storm low overhead, keeping boats secured

indicators.note: in a down entry overhead means this piece sits above the next

parts.note: to low is to moo like a cow
to storm is to rage

explanation.surface: A storm with low cloud overhead while boats are tied up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'low' looks like weather but is a cow's noise.
explanation.definitionFit: Moorage is the mooring of vessels, the place or act of tying boats up.

clue.text: Classic film's last word taps into anyone's heart

parts.note: a PS, postscript, is the final word in a letter

indicators.note: into means the taps go inside the heart letters
heart means the central letters of the word anyone

parts.note: C and H mark the cold and hot taps

explanation.surface: A classic movie's final line taps into the hearts of all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heart' takes the central pair of letters from anyone, and 'into' puts the two taps inside them.
explanation.definitionFit: Psycho is Alfred Hitchcock's celebrated 1960 thriller, a classic movie.

clue.text: Drink keeping staff close

indicators.note: keeping means holding the staff inside

parts.note: to sup is to drink
the crew is the staff of a ship

explanation.surface: A pub keeps its staff close.
explanation.walkthrough: 'close' is a verb: to screw up the eyes is to close them tightly.
explanation.definitionFit: To screw up the eyes means to squeeze them shut.

clue.text: Smelly old spot to squeeze poured forth

indicators.note: the spot piece squeezes the other piece into its middle

parts.note: a dot is a spot
liquid that poured forth ran

explanation.surface: An old pimple squeezed until it poured out something smelly.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective odorant means giving off scent, so smelly in a broad sense.

clue.text: Old rag in gift boxes

indicators.note: the phrase gift boxes the letters, holding them within

explanation.surface: An old rag tucked into a present.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gift boxes' looks like a noun phrase but is the container holding the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Aging means growing older, describing someone getting on in years.

clue.text: Drink with cool ingredient? Little appreciative word for food

indicators.note: an ingredient goes into a mixture, so this piece is put inside the drink

parts.note: cola is a soft drink
hip means cool, fashionable
ta is a short British way of saying thanks

explanation.surface: A trendy cocktail mixer, and a quick thank-you for the meal.
explanation.walkthrough: TA is informal British for 'thank you'.
explanation.definitionFit: A chipolata is a small thin sausage, a type of food.

clue.text: Expression I love: "Dusky shrouds"

indicators.note: shrouds means covers, so the dusky piece surrounds the love piece

parts.note: dusky light is dim
love is nil in tennis, the letter O

explanation.surface: A speaker quotes the phrase 'dusky shrouds'.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shrouds' wraps DIM round O.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom is a set phrase or turn of speech.

clue.text: Bunga bunga party ends for Silvio, power ebbing away

indicators.note: the ends of the following words are their final letters

explanation.surface: The wild parties end for Silvio Berlusconi as his power fades.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bunga bunga' parties were notorious at the home of Italian prime minister Silvio Berlusconi.
explanation.definitionFit: The bunga bunga parties were widely reported as wild sex parties, an orgy in tabloid terms.

clue.text: During winless season, foal at Ayr, perhaps, becoming juvenile

indicators.note: During means the foal piece sits within the season piece

parts.note: winter without WIN leaves TER
in Scots a foal is a wee nag, a little horse; Ayr is a Scottish town and racecourse

explanation.surface: A young horse at a Scottish course fails to win all winter.
explanation.walkthrough: Ayr is a Scottish town with a racecourse, hinting at Scots 'wee nag' for a young horse.
explanation.definitionFit: A tweenager is a child aged roughly ten to twelve, a juvenile between childhood and teens.
